issues.legal_issue: Taking possession of acquired land requires actual possession on the spot, with the sufficient act depending on the nature of the land.
material_facts: The land was waste or arable, lay fallow, and had no crop on it at the relevant time.
The acquisition officer directed the local revenue officer to take possession and deliver it to the public institution for which it was acquired.
The revenue officer went onto the land, inspected it to determine the area to be taken, and handed that area over to the institution.
The occupant was not present when possession was taken.
issues.conclusion: The inspection and determination of the area on the spot were sufficient, in the circumstances, to constitute actual possession. The occupant’s presence and advance notice of the precise time of taking possession were not legally necessary.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 9(1) and 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, possession for the purpose of vesting must be actual possession on the spot, not possession merely on paper or symbolic possession in the sense used in civil procedure. The act sufficient to take possession depends on the nature of the land; no universal act is prescribed. The owner’s or occupant’s presence and notice of the precise time are not legal requirements, though notice may be desirable to guard against paper possession.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: An authority was taking possession of land in a proceeding to acquire it for a public purpose.
predicates.authority_entered_land: The authority went onto the land as part of taking possession.
predicates.land_inspection_suited_to_its_nature: The land’s condition and use made inspection on the spot to identify the area being taken an act suited to taking possession.

issues.definition: When an authority enters land in an acquisition proceeding and performs an act suited to the land’s nature, actual possession is taken.

issues.legal_issue: An occupant’s resumption of possession after valid possession has been taken does not undo vesting or permit withdrawal from the acquisition.
material_facts: The revenue officer took possession on the spot of the waste or arable portion of the land and handed it over to the public institution.
The occupant entered or continued on the land after possession had been taken.
The government later directed withdrawal from acquisition of part of the land under the applicable withdrawal provision.
The land had been taken under the statutory urgency procedure.
issues.conclusion: The occupant’s resumption of possession did not undo the vesting of the land in the Government. Once possession had been taken, the Government or its commissioner could not withdraw from the acquisition of that land.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 16 and 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, land vests absolutely in the Government upon possession being taken, free from encumbrances. Section 48(1) does not permit withdrawal from acquisition of land after possession has been taken. The Court relied on State of Madhya Pradesh v. Vishnu Prasad Sharma and Lt. Governor of Himachal Pradesh v. Avinash Sharma for the rule that acquisition cannot be withdrawn after possession and vesting.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The matter concerns land being acquired by the Government for a public purpose.
predicates.actual_possession_taken: The Government validly took actual possession of the land on the spot.
predicates.occupant_resumed_possession: The former occupant entered or continued on the land after the Government had taken possession.

issues.definition: If the Government has taken actual possession in an acquisition proceeding, an occupant’s later return to the land does not make withdrawal from the acquisition available.
